links.outcome: Change in LLM risk estimates under equivalent unit conversion and field reordering
links.effect: Unit conversion changed raw risk by average absolute 0.93 percentage points for Qwen and 6.49 for Gemma; some representation changes improved error, others worsened it.
links.quote: Among 429 MOVER operations with a convertible laboratory value, unit conversion changed raw risk by an average absolute 0.93 percentage points for Qwen (0.75–1.14) and 6.49 for Gemma (5.77–7.20).

links.outcome: External Brier score change after applying source-derived logistic calibration to LLM risk estimates
links.effect: Source calibration increased external Brier scores by 0.01065 for Qwen (0.00791–0.01320) and 0.00200 for Gemma (0.00015–0.00377), i.e., calibration transfer was unsuccessful.
links.quote: Source calibration increased external Brier scores by 0.01065 for Qwen (95% interval 0.00791–0.01320) and 0.00200 for Gemma (0.00015–0.00377).

links.outcome: External AUC of LLMs compared with logistic regression and gradient boosting on same data
links.effect: External AUCs were 0.788 logistic regression, 0.782 gradient boosting, 0.656 Qwen and 0.722 Gemma; LLMs had weaker discrimination than simple models.
links.quote: External areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.788 for logistic regression, 0.782 for gradient boosting, 0.656 for Qwen and 0.722 for Gemma.

links.outcome: Performance of models transferred from source institution to external institution
links.effect: External AUC for LLMs was lower (Qwen 0.656, Gemma 0.722) than for conventional models (0.788, 0.782), and calibration transfer failed.
links.quote: In these two quantized models, lower aggregate probability error coexisted with weaker discrimination, unsuccessful calibration transfer and representation-dependent risks.
